A taste of Saigon
Feb 2019 • Family
A taste of Saigon, really fortunate that they were open on first day of Chinese New Year! Is at a back alley of District 3, easy access by Grab car, the owner were extremely friendly she even told us how to create our own sauce! We had seafood soup handmade fish cake, Jellyfish salad etc.. They also accommodate homestay on airdnd. I'm sure you won't get hungry their house is just right beside their stall. Great local food and service
Jul 2018 • Friends
Eating at this restaurant was a great start to our time in Vietnam. The owner was super friendly and spoke English very well. She showed us how to make our own traditional Vietnamese dipping sauce with kimchi, sugar, salt and chili for our different soups with noodles. Prices are very reasonable. If you want an authentic local dining experience we can definitely recommend this restaurant.
Love from Denmark.

Delicious Noodle Salad
Jun 2018 • Couples
Really clean and quaint restaurant tucked away in and alley of District 3. The dish is a seafood dish that comes as either a fresh noodle salad or noodle soup. I am allergic to prawns and the owner was very helpful in making sure there were none in my dish. We had the noodle salad and it was very good! we preferred it as a dish alone without the fish and broth that came with it. The owner is very good at English and explains exactly how to make your own sauce to accompany the dish and how to get the best flavors! Was a swell little restaurant:)

NOT as good as real Bun Quay in Phu Quoc Island.
Mar 2017 • Solo
I was travelling in Phu Quoc and I really fall in love with Bun Quay Phu Quoc which is near by The Night Market. 
However, this Bun Quay Sai Gon is totally different and NOT as good as its reputation. 
Bun Quay Phu Quoc's shrim and fish are really fresh and tasty. While the meat at Bun Quay Sai Gon is not that tender and fresh which is very disappointed. And they charge overprice. 40.000d is not a lot but it is NOT WORTH that price.

Fresh Homemade Noodles 🍜
Mar 2017 • Couples
There's a lot of soul in this homemade bowl of fish cake goodness. It's a part of Saigon that's worth trying and looking for. Definitely a hidden gem 💎 worth trying out. Noodles are made, pulled before being served with fish cakes, some flavorful broth, and finally topped with green onions, lime, 🌶 chilies and some mint. Most of all, it's very affordable and homemade. Michelle (the owner) is a great conversationist with a very warm heart. Always a pleasure to meet such good people.

Hidden Gem
Jan 2017
Tucked away in a little back alley in district 3 with no cars whizzing past, just the occasional moped, you'll fine Bun Quay Saigon. We are staying here as well so you might consider us biased but we are also very well versed in different foods and were given a full back story of how the noodles are made fresh for each order, you can ask for a range of spiciness and the way they make the shrimp and fish paste is quite unique! In our humble opinion it was light, fresh and authentic! Definitely worth dropping in and Michelle (the owner) speaks very good English!

Fresh and tasty
Dec 2016 • Couples
The restaurant offers fresh homemade noodles that are seriously unlike we have had in Vietnam (we spent 2.5 weeks travelling from south to north). We have eaten here multiple times and it does not disappoint. The broth is flavorful and delicious, the fish and shrimp are also handmade daily and you can tell that it's really fresh. The broth, noodles and not forgetting the side dipping sauce, makes this a truly delicious soup. The staff are friendly as well, the chef is hilarious and will engage even if English is not his language and Michelle is as friendly and sweet as it gets!!!
